author: Astrokillah
text:
josh1125 wrote: Well now that I'm back home it's back to work. I just discovered something that is pretty big for me. It may not be as big to some of you as it is for me, but I feel like in my mind, it adds another piece to the puzzle for me. In the chart below, there are two FLs to the left which I've labeled FL1 and FL 2. Price engulfed FL1, and I labeled that engulf Eng1. The target for Eng1 is FL2. After engulfing FL1, price immediately engulf our demand FL responsible for Eng1. So we label that Eng2. We now have an two engulfs, and we know that targets for each engulf. IF constantly state that price moves from FL to FL.

Hi Josh, your journal is nothing short of being my salvation.

I have been reading

various posts on RTM, and my brain is completely messed up to the point where when I start looking at a chart, I have no idea where to start looking!

The part where I

got stuck is PAZ, I have no idea how to make sense out of them. I have read many times that price moves from FL to FL. So I started looking for FL on my charts, and they are messy! Especially when price engulf a level, but then immediately make a big retrace, so we end up with big FLs on our chart, overlapped, and price could range within these big FLs for a long time without breaking the outer edges. Anyway, enough rambling. What your journal has taught me is instead of looking at FL, I should first learn how to make PAZ using space between FTRs.

I am looking at your post #449, and it is making so much sense, and makes me realize the importance of marking our charts properly, because one missing FTR, or FL, could lead to a different conclusion. I know that this is an old post, and you might have new understanding and are looking at things differently now. I was wondering, would you consider the space between a DP and an FTR a PAZ too? Conceptually, what I meant is this:

It is a well-established rule in RTM that a PAZ is between two FTR, in the diagram above, I 'cheated' a little, because the rules say an FTR is the MPL of an FL. And an FL is created AFTER the break of a key SR level or another FL. I haven't seen FTR being associated with DP at all. What I am questioning, is why do we leave DP out of the picture completely, because we have seen how price bounces off DPs too.

And it is with this question in mind, that when I see this chart, I am thinking about this, see my little comment in pink color:

So price engulfed FL edge 1, and we have space until it reached FL2 above. Then price engulfed south of a small FL is not visible on this 30-min timeframe. So we now have space to the south.

Question, is where should be the proper target to the south? Is it at the DP (A) or the FL below (B)?

I am sorry if I am writing too much crap here!! Hope you don't mind. Thank you very much. AK

author: josh1125
text:
Sorry for such a late reply, things have been really hectic lately. For me, decision points are important, but then again they aren't. I've noticed that most decision points are going to give a bounce in price, but FL's are where the real orders lay. Many times, decision points are used to create BSZs. They are normally extremely visible to every trader, and normally happens somewhere near a FL. I very rarely will take a trade from a decision point. When taking trades, only decision points that matter are the ones that occur inside of FLs. For me, decision points are good levels to use for targets.
